correctness.rationale: The exact sharp norm and optimal stability gap for every q>q_c are Theorems 1.2--1.3 of Xu, arXiv:2610.19648, read at the actual source. Fixed-order Hankel expansions from DLMF 10.17 yield identical moment poles B_d/(q-q_c); periodic zero-mean integration by parts proves uniform convergence of their difference at q_c. Theorem 3.9 of Xu proves positive integrals on every complete adjacent Bessel-zero cell for all q>2; at q_c>2 this makes the convergent difference Delta_d strictly positive. A mean-value limit gives the 1/d exponent and coefficient. Numerical tests of nine finite-q comparisons are only corroborative; the limits rely on proofs.

This is a qualified current-evidence originality assessment, not an independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The strong-type endpoint makes every individual harmonic moment infinite, so the exact sharp stability constant has an a priori uncertain singular behavior. Identifying a finite positive adjacent-mode cancellation, a dimension-dependent exponent 1/d for its absolute collapse, and an exact linear relative collapse quantifies stability degradation across all d>=3. This is a natural continuum restriction operator with immediate significance to sharp extremizer stability; it is not an arbitrary computed slice, tautological substitute, or numerical-only statement. No independent audit has been performed.
